messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: kv-cache eviction rate > 3x baseline for int8 model group in us-west-2. Paging spike observed, p95 latency for streaming generation up ~450ms. Trigger: quantized kernel path (int8/awq) falling back to larger KV sizes. Incident page: https://redwood.incidents/1864123456 :rotating_light:

Miguel Torres: seeing the same in Grafana. eviction/sec jumped at 03:14 UTC, cache size for model gptq-small-int8 reported ~2.8x expected. continuous-batching queue depth also up.

Alex Chen: tagging @priya — this smells like kernel selection regression we rolled in last night (A/B kernel selector change). Any quick rollback?

Priya Rao: I was on that change, yes. We tuned selector to prefer quant kernels for smaller batch sizes; it may be misclassifying seq length distribution and producing huge KV footprints. Rolling back to previous selector is possible but will require a config push.

Janet (CS): FYI, two customers reported increased 503s on chat endpoints (Acme and TidalHealth). CS is on the line with Acme. We need ETA for mitigation.

Miguel Torres: mitigation plan I propose: 1) reduce continuous-batching max window for int8 variants to 10ms 2) temporarily increase KV eviction threshold to reduce immediate paging 3) force kernel-selector override to prefer fallback kernel for models exceeding kv-size threshold 4) alert customers.

Alex Chen: agree. Steps and commands:
```bash
# throttle batching for int8 model group
redwoodctl config set inference.models.int8.batch_window_ms 10 --region us-west-2
# raise eviction threshold from 70% -> 85% on cache shards
redwoodctl cache set eviction_threshold 0.85 --shards usw2-*
# add kernel selector override rule
redwoodctl runtime override-kernel --model-group int8 --selector "if kv_size>256MB then prefer: kernel-fallback" --region us-west-2
```
I can push these; will coordinate safe rollout. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Deploy job started: config-change/1864123456. Logs: https://ci.redwood/deploys/1864123456

Priya Rao: note — forcing fallback kernel will increase per-token CPU but should shrink KV entries (we think kv-encoding difference between quant kernels is causing large key/value blob).

Miguel Torres: applying eviction_threshold change now. spool up extra monitoring: kv_evictions_per_min, paging_io_iops, streaming_p95.

Alex Chen: batching throttle applied and propagated to edge nodes. Observability: queue depth dropped 40% and p95 reduced ~120ms within 3 minutes.

Priya Rao: kernel-selector override in place on canary pool. Observed canary: kv size per session reduced ~60%. no errors. Preparing to promote to 50% traffic.

Janet (CS): telling Acme this is being mitigated, CS asked for rough ETA. I gave them 30 minutes and asked for callback.

Miguel Torres: promote override to 50% now. watch for CPU spike and request latencies.

Alex Chen: override promoted. CPU increased ~15% on affected nodes, but paging dropped sharply and eviction/sec stabilized near baseline.

Priya Rao: promoting to 100% on int8 model group. Doing a rolling push.

deploy-bot: Deploy job success: config-change/1864123456 promoted -> all regions.

Miguel Torres: current status: eviction/sec back to normal, paging IOPS down 70%, p95 streaming latency back within SLO. Customer reports pending but Acme confirmed a big improvement.

Janet (CS): Acme says error rate dropped to near zero. TidalHealth still seeing a few timeouts; escalated to eng for deeper trace.

Alex Chen: root-cause hypothesis: kernel-selector A/B tweak caused quant path to be chosen for sessions where kv footprint would explode (edge-case distribution), combined with continuous-batching heuristics that increased KV persistence. The quant kernels had an unwelcome kv-serialization size regression.

Priya Rao: short-term fix = selector override + batching throttle + eviction tweak. Medium-term: revert selector change and roll a safer heuristic; investigate quant kernel serializer for AWQ/GPTQ int8 to understand kv blob growth.

Miguel Torres: handoff: I'm stepping out in 20m. @Anna Lee will take oncall watch for 6 hours. Anna, monitor paging, kv_evictions_per_min, and customer tickets; Priya will own kernel patch and Alex will own rollout telemetry + postmortem.

Anna Lee: on it. will post updates every 30m and escalate if paging > baseline*1.2 or p95 > SLO.

Priya Rao: initial debugging notes: suspected change was in kernel selection model v2. Patch candidates: (a) tighten threshold logic for small batch quant selection, (b) fallback to 16-bit kernel for sessions with >128MB kv predicted. I'll prepare a PR and include test harness for kv-size sim.

Alex Chen: recording action items in #postmortems: 1) revert A/B selector or roll safer variant 2) kernel serializer audit for int8/awq/gptq paths 3) add automatic kv_size prediction to selector to avoid large sessions 4) add paging grace metric/auto-throttle 5) CS follow-up for impacted customers.

Miguel Torres: filing incident ticket INC-1864123456 and tagging SRE+ML. Will update timeline and attach timeseries.

Janet (CS): thanks team. continuing customer comms. will confirm TidalHealth behavior after Anna's watch. :pray: 

Anna Lee: quick check-in 30m: metrics stable, small lingering 5xx for one shard; routing team diverting traffic from that shard to spare capacity. will follow up with a sticky ticket.

Miguel Torres: thank you. I'll compile initial report and hand off to Priya for root-cause writeup. Closing the on-call handoff here.

Priya Rao: PR for selector revert coming in next 2 hours, will include canary plan.

Alex Chen: will collect telemetry snapshots for pre/post rollback for the postmortem.

incident-bot: Incident INC-1864123456: mitigated -> monitoring. Severity: Sev2. Handoff complete to Anna Lee for watch, owners: Priya (kernel), Alex (telemetry), Miguel (SRE lead).
